turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
“Hello, doctor. I’m here for my annual check-up, but I’ve also noticed a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the back of my left hand. It doesn’t hurt and I don’t feel any tenderness.”
How long has this rough, scaly patch been present on your hand?
“Since about a few months ago, doctor—though I can’t recall the exact first day it appeared.”
Is the patch raised above the skin like a bump, or is it relatively flat, and what color would you say it appears—skin-colored, pink, red, or brown?
“It feels a bit raised, like a rough patch above the skin rather than completely flat. The color looks mostly pinkish to skin-toned, not bright red or very dark.”
How old are you, and do you have a history of significant sun exposure to your hands through work or outdoor activities?
“I’m 65 years old, and I do spend time outdoors walking and sunbathing, so I’ve had regular sun exposure on my hands.”
Does the lesion feel hard or firm when you press on it, or is it just rough on the surface?
“It’s mostly just rough on the surface rather than clearly hard or firm when I press it, doctor.”
What is the approximate size of this patch, and do you have any other similar spots on your hands, forearms, face, or scalp?
“About the size of a small coin, doctor—roughly 1 to 2 centimeters. I haven’t noticed similar spots elsewhere on my hands, face, forearms, or scalp.”
Has the patch ever bled, ulcerated, or shown any rapid growth, and does the scale ever flake off and then return?

“No, doctor—it hasn’t bled or ulcerated, and it hasn’t grown rapidly. The surface does seem to get a little scaly at times, but I don’t see it forming an open sore or completely clearing and then coming right back.”
[DDX] Actinic Keratosis, Squamous Cell Carcinoma, Seborrheic Keratosis, Bowen Disease (Squamous Cell Carcinoma in situ), Verruca Vulgaris
